# The boot path & kernel-crash forensics 🔴

**Goal.** Own every stage from firmware to a captured kernel panic: interrupt the boot loader, force and dissect a crash, meet the firmware that answers back at a Forth prompt (twice — two rival implementations of the same standard), turn that prompt into a forensics workbench of your own words, then replace the firmware's boot logic with Linux itself.

**Audience:** you can bring up a Debian VM; comfort with GRUB/serial helps  
**Effort:** ⏱ half-day+  
**Prerequisites:** none

| # | Lab | You'll learn | Checkpoint (observable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [`vm-examples/vm-debian-amd64.toml`](../vm-examples/vm-debian-amd64.toml) | a baseline KVM cloud VM to experiment on. | `lab-vm.sh ssh` logs you in. |
| 2 | [`root-password-reset`](../root-password-reset/) 🔑 | console/boot access equals root — via `init=/bin/bash` or `rd.break`. | reset root on the VM; the OLD password is rejected and the NEW one works; `/proc/cmdline` proves your GRUB edit took (mind the serial char-drop gotcha). |
| 3 | [`kdump-kexec-lab`](../kdump-kexec-lab/) | arm kdump, force a panic, let the kexec capture kernel save a vmcore, then read it in `crash`. | `echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger` yields a ~42 MB vmcore in `/var/crash`; `crash` `sym` resolves the panic to `test-module.c:8`. |
| 4 | [`open-firmware-forth-to-boot`](../open-firmware-forth-to-boot/) 📟 | the rival answer to firmware modularity, live: IEEE 1275's `ok` prompt is a Forth REPL on the bare machine — walk the device tree, patch the running firmware, and make it boot Linux; also as a coreboot payload. | `3 4 + .` prints `7` at the `ok` prompt over serial (`smoke-ofw.sh` PASSes both flavors); `showcase-forth-to-boot.sh` ends `PASS: ... booted Linux to u-root` after hand-staging the initrd at the prompt. |
| 5 | [`open-firmware-debugs-itself`](../open-firmware-debugs-itself/) 🔬 | the same `ok` prompt, now as a forensics workbench: write a Forth DSL (a vocabulary, not a parser) that turns "Can't open boot device" into a per-entry diagnosis, traces the boot path through the firmware's OWN defer hooks, walks PCI config space and checks itself against QEMU, and runs a driver that arrived as bytecode on a card's option ROM. Then put the DSL INSIDE the ROM as a dropin so it needs no media, hook `banner-` so the power-on autoboot traces itself, and single-step the firmware's own debugger — while it decompiles itself with `see`. | `smoke-dsl.sh all` PASSes every mode (and again with `coreboot`); `showcase-diagnose-a-broken-boot.sh` ends `PASS: diagnosed a boot failure the firmware only called "Can't open boot device", repaired the broken alias live, and verified the repair`; `dev /pci ls` shows a node named `fcode-card` that the CARD named itself; after `build-dropin-rom.sh --boot-hook`, a boot with NO media prints `#T open …` lines before the first `ok` prompt with nothing typed.<br>🔎 auto-checkable → marker `PASS: all vocabularies verified` |
| 6 | [`openbios-the-rival-that-shipped`](../openbios-the-rival-that-shipped/) ☎️ | the SAME standard, the OTHER implementation — OpenBIOS, the one still shipping (QEMU's default ppc/sparc firmware). The contrast IS the lesson: where the frozen rival got fixed live at the prompt, this maintained C loader gets fixed in a patch — booting Linux needs no `memmap=`, no hand-staged initrd, no zero-page poke. | `smoke-openbios.sh` PASSes all three tracks (multiboot/coreboot/ppc); the ppc one proves the running firmware is OUR build (banner date ≠ QEMU's bundled blob); `showcase-rival-boots-linux.sh` ends `PASS: the rival boots Linux ... reached u-root` from one `boot` line. |
| 7 | [`open-firmware-native-habitats`](../open-firmware-native-habitats/) 🏝️ | the same DSL, in the habitats where the standard actually shipped — Sun SPARC and Apple PowerPC. A vocabulary is portable; an implementation is not: the diagnosis ladder ports, a fifth rung is forced because native `boot-device` entries carry device arguments, and the tracers cannot port at all because OpenBIOS declares no `defer` on its boot path — so the lab IMPLEMENTS the standard's empty `patch` (7.5.3.3) and rewrites the call sites instead — then `.calls` (7.5.3.1, also empty) from the same walk, and finally the real fix: both baked into `forth/debugging/firmware.fs` and the firmware rebuilt, because loading them at runtime only SHADOWS the stubs. Then the finding that reframes it: each habitat opens exactly ONE door for getting a vocabulary in — NVRAM on Apple, a mounted disc on Sun — and no single door works on both. | `smoke-habitat.sh all sparc32` = 9 PASS, `all ppc` = 6 PASS + 3 justified SKIP; booting ppc with `-prom-env nvramrc=…` prints `ofdiag loaded` ABOVE `Welcome to OpenBIOS` (pre-probe, straight off the NVRAM chip), and `why-no-boot` then diagnoses all three of Apple's `hd:,\:tbxi` boot entries at the `0 >` prompt. With the autotrace script in NVRAM instead, `#T load-begin`/`#T open`/`#T load-end` appear BEFORE the first prompt — the power-on autoboot tracing itself on a firmware that ships no tracepoint.<br>🔎 auto-checkable → marker `PASS: ladder (ppc)` |
| 8 | [`linuxboot-uefi-kexec`](../linuxboot-uefi-kexec/) | firmware is just software: u-root as the firmware's `init`, which `kexec`s the real OS. | two 'Welcome to u-root!' banners + a `[0.000000]` clock reset (Tier C fast-loop → Tier B UKI on OVMF → Tier A coreboot ROM); the System-Transparency capstone boots ONLY a signed OSPKG and refuses a rogue one. |

### Optional side-quests

- [`systemd261-nixos-measured-boot`](../systemd261-nixos-measured-boot/) — boot *integrity* rather than boot *recovery*: a Nix-built NixOS on **systemd 261** measured into a (soft)TPM, deployed on-disk over iPXE, with staged rollout by machine-ID (`ConditionFraction=`) and storage sealed to the measured state (TPM2 LUKS bound to PCR 7+11 + a PCR-quote attestation stub). Spikes A–G verified — measured-os MET on a dm-verity+UKI image, sealed LUKS unseals only on the expected PCRs; honest gap: `RestrictFileSystemAccess=` isn't in nixpkgs' systemd 261. See its PLAN.md.
